questions.question: What is the histological classification of lupus nephritis showing mesangial proliferation with immune deposits visible only by immunofluorescence?
questions.explanation: Class II of the ISN/RPS classification corresponds to mesangial proliferative nephritis with mesangial hypercellularity and immune deposits visible only by immunofluorescence or electron microscopy, without active glomerular involvement.

questions.question: What class of lupus nephritis is characterized by segmental, focal lesions affecting less than 50% of the glomeruli?
questions.explanation: Class III (focal lupus nephritis) presents segmental or global glomerular involvement in less than 50% of the glomeruli, differentiating it from class IV, which affects 50% or more.

questions.question: What is the type of lupus nephritis that is most frequently associated with nephrotic syndrome and has the worst long-term renal prognosis?
questions.explanation: Class V (membranous) presents with proteinuria in the nephrotic range and, although it has a better prognosis than the proliferative ones, it can progress to chronic kidney disease if not treated appropriately.

questions.question: What class of lupus nephritis requires aggressive immunosuppressive treatment with cyclophosphamide or mycophenolate according to current guidelines?
questions.explanation: Class IV (diffuse) is an active proliferative glomerulonephritis that affects ≥50% of the glomeruli and requires induction with cyclophosphamide or mycophenolate mofetil, along with corticosteroids, to avoid irreversible renal damage.

questions.question: ¿Qué clase de nefritis lúpica se define por la presencia de más del 50% de glomérulos afectados, ya sea segmentaria o globalmente?
questions.explanation: La clase IV (difusa) se caracteriza por afectación de ≥50% de los glomérulos, con patrón segmentario o global, y puede presentar crescentes, necrosis o esclerosis, siendo la más agresiva de las formas proliferativas.

questions.question: ¿Qué clase de nefritis lúpica representa la fase esclerosante avanzada con esclerosis glomerular global en más del 90% de los glomérulos y sin actividad?
questions.explanation: Class VI corresponds to advanced sclerosing lupus nephritis, with global sclerosis in >90% of the glomeruli, without evidence of immunological activity; Treatment focuses on conservative management of chronic kidney disease.

questions.question: What is the main indication for performing renal biopsy in a patient with systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation: Renal biopsy is indicated in persistent proteinuria greater than 500 mg/day, especially with active urinary sediment, to confirm lupus nephritis and classify the histological class that guides treatment.

questions.question: In a patient with lupus and proteinuria in the nephrotic range, what additional finding justifies immediate renal biopsy?
questions.explanation: Acute elevation of serum creatinine without another cause, together with proteinuria, suggests active glomerulonephritis and requires urgent renal biopsy to decide immunosuppressive therapy.

questions.question: Which of the following laboratory parameters constitutes a formal indication for renal biopsy in lupus?
questions.explanation: The presence of granular casts in the urinary sediment is an indicator of active nephritis and, together with proteinuria or renal deterioration, justifies renal biopsy to classify the lesion.

questions.question: ¿En qué situación clínica la biopsia renal en lupus puede diferirse o evitarse?
questions.explanation: La proteinuria subnefrótica sin sedimento activo ni deterioro de la función renal no siempre requiere biopsia inmediata; puede manejarse inicialmente de forma conservadora y biopsiar si hay progresión.

questions.question: Un paciente con lupus presenta proteinuria de 1.2 g/día y microhematuria. ¿Qué clase histológica esperaría encontrar en la biopsia renal?
questions.explanation: La nefritis lúpica clase III (focal proliferativa) se manifiesta típicamente con proteinuria y hematuria, y requiere biopsia para confirmar la actividad y guiar tratamiento inmunosupresor.

questions.question: What is the main objective of performing a kidney biopsy in a patient with active lupus?
questions.explanation: Renal biopsy in lupus seeks to classify nephritis (I to VI) and evaluate activity and chronicity indices, which defines immunosuppressive therapy and renal prognosis.

questions.question: What is the recommended induction treatment for class III/IV lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: La terapia de inducción estándar incluye glucocorticoides más micofenolato de mofetilo o ciclofosfamida intravenosa. El micofenolato es una opción de primera línea comparable a ciclofosfamida, pero la pregunta pide el tratamiento de inducción recomendado en general.

questions.question: Which drug is reserved as maintenance therapy in class III/IV lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Maintenance therapy is performed with mycophenolate mofetil or azathioprine. Cyclophosphamide is used in induction, not in long-term maintenance due to toxicity; Rituximab and belimumab are not first line maintenance.

questions.question: What is the minimum recommended duration of maintenance therapy in lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Maintenance therapy should be continued for at least 36 months after induction, according to guidelines, before tapering is considered. Shorter duration is associated with greater risk of renal relapse.

questions.question: What finding in renal biopsy indicates activity in class IV lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: La clase IV se define por proliferación endocapilar difusa, a menudo con depósitos subendoteliales. Esclerosis, atrofia y fibrosis son lesiones crónicas, no actividad.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la primera línea de tratamiento si hay respuesta insuficiente a inducción inicial?
questions.explanation: En caso de respuesta insuficiente, se recomienda cambiar a la otra terapia de inducción (si inició con micofenolato, usar ciclofosfamida y viceversa). Rituximab se considera en casos refractarios, no como primera alternativa.

questions.question: ¿Qué comorbilidad obliga a ajustar la dosis de ciclofosfamida en nefritis lúpica?
questions.explanation: La ciclofosfamida se elimina por vía renal; en insuficiencia renal crónica se requiere reducción de dosis para evitar toxicidad. Las otras comorbilidades no contraindican ni modifican su dosis de forma directa.

questions.question: What is the first-line drug for induction in class IV lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: In diffuse proliferative lupus nephritis (class IV), mycophenolate mofetil is a first-line induction option, comparable to cyclophosphamide, and is preferred in certain settings due to its safety profile.

questions.question: What mechanism explains the effectiveness of cyclophosphamide in inducing lupus nephritis?
options: Aumenta la actividad de células T reguladoras
questions.explanation: La ciclofosfamida es un agente alquilante que inhibe la proliferación linfocitaria, reduciendo la producción de autoanticuerpos y la inflamación renal en lupus activo.

questions.question: ¿Qué dosis de ciclofosfamida se usa en el régimen Euro-Lupus para inducción?
questions.explanation: The Euro-Lupus regimen administers 500 mg of intravenous cyclophosphamide every two weeks for six doses, designed to reduce toxicity while maintaining efficacy in lupus nephritis.

questions.question: What is the typical duration of mycophenolate induction therapy in lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: La fase de inducción con micofenolato mofetilo suele durar al menos 6 meses, tras los cuales se evalúa respuesta renal y se decide pasar a terapia de mantenimiento.

questions.question: ¿Qué efecto adverso grave obliga a monitorizar recuento sanguíneo durante inducción con ciclofosfamida?
questions.explanation: Cyclophosphamide causes dose-dependent myelosuppression, so monitoring of leukocytes and neutrophils is required to prevent serious infections during induction.

questions.question: What consideration contraindicates the use of mycophenolate in patients with lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Mycophenolate is teratogenic and is contraindicated in pregnancy or in women planning to conceive without effective contraception; A negative pregnancy test is required before starting.

questions.question: What is the first-line drug for maintenance in lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Mycophenolate mofetil is one of the first-line agents for the maintenance of lupus nephritis, along with azathioprine, according to international guidelines.

questions.question: What alternative to mycophenolate is accepted in the maintenance of lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Azathioprine is a valid maintenance option, especially in patients who desire pregnancy or are intolerant to mycophenolate, supported by clinical guidelines.

questions.question: Why is mycophenolate preferred over azathioprine in maintenance?
questions.explanation: Estudios comparativos muestran que micofenolato tiene mayor eficacia en prevenir recaídas y lograr remisión renal sostenida en nefritis lúpica, aunque con más efectos adversos.

questions.question: ¿Qué situación favorece elegir azatioprina en mantenimiento?
questions.explanation: Azatioprina es segura en el embarazo, a diferencia de micofenolato que es teratogénico, por lo que se prefiere en mujeres con plan reproductivo.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la duración mínima recomendada de mantenimiento en nefritis lúpica?
questions.explanation: The guidelines recommend maintaining immunosuppression for at least 36 months after induction, to reduce the risk of renal relapse and progression to renal failure.

questions.question: ¿Qué efecto adverso limita el uso crónico de micofenolato?
questions.explanation: La mielosupresión, especialmente leucopenia, es un efecto adverso relevante del micofenolato que requiere control hematológico periódico durante el tratamiento.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el valor de proteinuria en 24 horas que define respuesta renal completa en lupus?
questions.explanation: Complete renal response in lupus nephritis is defined with proteinuria less than 0.5 g/day and stable or improved renal function, without active urinary sediment.

questions.question: What renal function criterion is required to consider a complete renal response?
options: Glomerular filtration rate greater than 90 ml/min
Absence of proteinuria on reagent strip
Normal serum creatinine in all patients
questions.explanation: Complete renal response requires stability or improvement in serum creatinine compared to the baseline value, without the need to normalize it in all patients.

questions.question: What finding in the urinary sediment indicates the absence of renal lupus activity?
questions.explanation: Complete renal response requires inactive urinary sediment, defined as fewer than 5 erythrocytes per field and the absence of blood or granular casts.

questions.question: What additional parameter is included in the evaluation of complete renal response?
questions.explanation: Although biomarkers such as anti-DNA and complement are used, the complete renal response is confirmed with a low histological activity index in control biopsy.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el tiempo mínimo de mantenimiento de los criterios para considerar respuesta renal completa?
questions.explanation: La respuesta renal completa en nefritis lúpica debe mantenerse durante al menos 6 meses consecutivos para evitar confundir mejoría transitoria con remisión real.

questions.question: ¿Qué valor de proteinuria/creatinina en orina (mg/g) equivale al criterio de proteinuria de 0.5 g/día?
questions.explanation: En la práctica, una relación proteinuria/creatinina en muestra aislada menor de 500 mg/g se considera equivalente a proteinuria de 24 horas menor de 0.5 g.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation: Class IV lupus nephritis (diffuse proliferative) is the most common and aggressive, and frequently presents as nephrotic syndrome. Class V (membranous) also causes nephrotic proteinuria, but is less common than class IV.

questions.question: What histological finding is characteristic of class V lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: La nefritis lúpica clase V (membranosa) se caracteriza por engrosamiento difuso de la membrana basal glomerular debido a depósitos subepiteliales. Las opciones 1, 3 y 4 corresponden a patrones proliferativos (clase IV o III).

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el tratamiento de primera línea para nefritis lúpica clase IV con síndrome nefrótico?
questions.explanation: Mycophenolate mofetil is a first-line option along with glucocorticoids for proliferative lupus nephritis (class III/IV). Cyclophosphamide is also valid, but mycophenolate is preferred due to its similar safety and efficacy profile.

questions.question: Which antibody is most associated with active lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: Los anticuerpos anti-dsDNA son específicos de lupus y se correlacionan con actividad renal, especialmente en nefritis proliferativa. Anti-Ro, anti-La y anti-histona no son marcadores de nefritis lúpica activa.

questions.question: ¿Qué porcentaje de pacientes con lupus eritematoso sistémico desarrolla nefritis?
questions.explanation: Approximately 40-60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus present nephritis, and many of them present with nephrotic syndrome. This high prevalence justifies regular screening for proteinuria.

questions.question: ¿Qué dato de laboratorio es más útil para diferenciar síndrome nefrótico lúpico de otras causas?
questions.explanation: La hipocomplementemia (C3 y C4 bajos) es característica de nefritis lúpica activa por consumo de complemento. Los otros hallazgos son comunes a cualquier síndrome nefrótico, no específicos de lupus.

questions.question: Which finding in the urinary sediment is characteristic of active lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: In active lupus nephritis, especially in proliferative classes such as class III and IV, blood casts together with dysmorphic hematuria indicate active glomerular damage. Hyaline casts are nonspecific and do not reflect inflammatory activity.

questions.question: What pathophysiological mechanism explains glomerular hematuria in lupus?
questions.explanation: Glomerular hematuria in lupus is due to deposits of immune complexes in the mesangium and subendothelium, which activate complement and cause inflammation and rupture of the glomerular basement membrane. The other mechanisms are not typical of lupus.

questions.question: What is the next step in the management of a patient with lupus and active hematuria?
questions.explanation: Ante hematuria glomerular activa con cilindros celulares, se debe realizar biopsia renal para clasificar la nefritis lúpica y guiar tratamiento inmunosupresor. No hay indicación de antibióticos ni de diálisis sin datos de falla avanzada.

questions.question: ¿Qué clase de nefritis lúpica se asocia más frecuentemente con hematuria y cilindros hemáticos?
questions.explanation: La nefritis lúpica clase IV (difusa proliferativa) es la más grave y frecuentemente presenta sedimento activo con hematuria y cilindros hemáticos. Las clases I y II tienen sedimento generalmente inactivo, y la V suele cursar con proteinuria sin hematuria.

questions.question: ¿Qué tratamiento de primera línea se indica en nefritis lúpica clase IV con actividad?
questions.explanation: Induction therapy for class IV lupus nephritis includes mycophenolate mofetil or cyclophosphamide combined with corticosteroids. Azathioprine is not used in induction, and rituximab is second line. Cyclophosphamide is always associated with corticosteroids.

questions.question: What additional finding supports glomerular origin of hematuria in lupus?
questions.explanation: Acanthocytes (dysmorphic red blood cells) are specific markers of glomerular hematuria. Monomorphic hematuria suggests a nonglomerular origin, and fat casts are associated with proteinuria, not active hematuria.

questions.question: What pathophysiological mechanism explains the low levels of C3 and C4 in lupus kidney flare?
questions.explanation: In the renal flare of lupus, circulating immune complexes are deposited in the glomerulus and activate the classical complement pathway, consuming C3 and C4 and producing hypocomplementemia.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es la causa más frecuente de hipocomplementemia en pacientes con nefritis lúpica activa?
questions.explanation: La nefritis lúpica activa se caracteriza por depósito de inmunocomplejos que activan la vía clásica del complemento, consumiendo C3 y C4 y causando hipocomplementemia.

questions.question: Which laboratory finding is typical in a patient with lupus renal flare?
questions.explanation: Durante el brote renal lúpico, la activación del complemento por inmunocomplejos consume C3 y C4, por lo que ambos suelen estar disminuidos en sangre.

questions.question: What parameter is useful to monitor the response to treatment in lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: The normalization of C3 and C4 levels correlates with the remission of the renal flare, making them useful biomarkers to monitor the therapeutic response.

questions.question: What class of lupus nephritis is most often associated with severe hypocomplementemia?
questions.explanation: Class III (focal) and class IV (diffuse) lupus nephritis are the most proliferative and are associated with greater complement consumption, manifesting with low C3 and C4.

questions.question: What treatment is indicated in the first line for lupus kidney flare with low C3 and C4?
questions.explanation: Mycophenolate mofetil is a first-line therapy for active lupus nephritis, along with glucocorticoids, especially in proliferative classes.

questions.question: Which autoantibody is most specific for the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation: El anti-Sm es el autoanticuerpo más específico para el diagnóstico de lupus eritematoso sistémico, aunque su sensibilidad es baja, aproximadamente del 30%. Los anti-dsDNA son menos específicos pero se asocian con actividad renal.

questions.question: ¿Con qué manifestación clínica se asocia principalmente la presencia de anticuerpos anti-dsDNA?
questions.explanation: Los anticuerpos anti-dsDNA se asocian fuertemente con nefritis lúpica, especialmente en la forma activa y difusa. Su título suele correlacionarse con la actividad renal, por lo que se monitorean en el seguimiento de pacientes con lupus.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es el tratamiento de primera línea para la nefritis lúpica proliferativa activa?
questions.explanation: La ciclofosfamida es uno de los tratamientos de primera línea para la nefritis lúpica proliferativa activa, junto con micofenolato de mofetilo. La elección entre ambos depende de factores como la severidad y la disponibilidad, pero ambos son válidos como terapia inicial.

questions.question: In a patient with active lupus and suspected nephritis, which laboratory finding is most indicative of renal activity?
questions.explanation: La proteinuria en rango nefrótico (>3.5 g/día) es un hallazgo clásico de nefritis lúpica activa, especialmente en la clase IV. Aunque la elevación de anti-dsDNA y el consumo de complemento son marcadores de actividad, la proteinuria es el indicador renal más directo y cuantificable.

questions.question: Which antibody is considered a marker of disease activity in lupus?
questions.explanation: Los anticuerpos anti-dsDNA son los principales marcadores de actividad en lupus eritematoso sistémico. Sus títulos aumentan durante los brotes, especialmente cuando hay compromiso renal, y disminuyen con el tratamiento efectivo.

questions.question: Which combination of autoantibodies is highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.explanation: The simultaneous presence of anti-Sm and anti-dsDNA is highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus, as both are key serological markers. While anti-Sm is very specific, anti-dsDNA is associated with activity and nephritis, and their combination strengthens the diagnosis.

questions.question: What is the main pathophysiological mechanism of arterial hypertension in active lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: In lupus nephritis, glomerular inflammation and immune complex deposition reduce renal perfusion, activating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, raising blood pressure.

questions.question: What finding defines nephrotic range proteinuria in a patient with lupus?
options: Proteinuria de 500 mg en muestra aislada
questions.explanation: Nephrotic range proteinuria is defined as protein excretion greater than 3.5 g in 24-hour urine, a key criterion for classifying the severity of lupus nephritis.

questions.question: What is the first-line antihypertensive treatment in a patient with lupus and persistent proteinuria?
questions.explanation: ACEIs or ARBs are first-line drugs due to their antiproteinuric and renoprotective effect, independent of their antihypertensive action, essential in lupus nephritis.

questions.question: ¿Qué meta de presión arterial se recomienda en pacientes con lupus y proteinuria significativa?
questions.explanation: Las guías recomiendan meta de presión arterial menor de 130/80 mmHg en pacientes con enfermedad renal crónica y proteinuria para retardar la progresión del daño renal.

questions.question: ¿Qué clase de nefritis lúpica se asocia con mayor frecuencia a hipertensión arterial severa?
questions.explanation: La nefritis lúpica clase IV (difusa proliferativa) es la más agresiva, con proliferación endocapilar difusa y necrosis, causando hipertensión severa y deterioro rápido de la función renal.

questions.question: What finding in the urinary sediment supports renal activity in lupus?
questions.explanation: En la nefritis lúpica activa, la presencia de cilindros granulosos o eritrocitarios junto con hematuria refleja proliferación glomerular e inflamación, indicando actividad inmunológica.

questions.question: What is the main mechanism of action of rituximab in lupus nephritis?
options: Bloqueo del factor de necrosis tumoral
questions.explanation: Rituximab es un anticuerpo monoclonal quimérico que se une al antígeno CD20 presente en linfocitos B, provocando su depleción. Esta acción reduce la producción de autoanticuerpos y la presentación antigénica en la nefritis lúpica, siendo útil como terapia de segunda línea en casos refractarios o recaídas.

questions.question: En la nefritis lúpica proliferativa difusa (clase IV), el rituximab se considera principalmente como:
options: Primera línea en todos los pacientes
Terapia de rescate en casos refractarios
questions.explanation: El rituximab no es tratamiento de primera línea en la nefritis lúpica; se reserva como terapia de rescate o segunda línea en pacientes con respuesta insuficiente, intolerancia o contraindicación a los esquemas convencionales con ciclofosfamida o micofenolato, según las guías de práctica clínica.

questions.question: ¿Qué combinación farmacológica se emplea habitualmente junto al rituximab en la nefritis lúpica?
questions.explanation: En la nefritis lúpica, el rituximab se asocia a glucocorticoides y a un inmunosupresor de mantenimiento como el micofenolato de mofetilo. Esta combinación busca maximizar la depleción de linfocitos B y controlar la actividad inflamatoria renal sin aumentar excesivamente la toxicidad.

questions.question: ¿Cuál es un efecto adverso grave asociado al uso de rituximab en pacientes con nefritis lúpica?
questions.explanation: El síndrome de liberación de citoquinas es una complicación grave, aunque infrecuente, del rituximab, caracterizado por fiebre, hipotensión y disfunción multiorgánica. Otros efectos adversos relevantes incluyen reacciones infusionales, infecciones oportunistas y leucoencefalopatía multifocal progresiva.

questions.question: What laboratory parameter is monitored to evaluate the response to rituximab in lupus nephritis?
questions.explanation: El recuento de linfocitos B CD19 es un biomarcador farmacodinámico útil para confirmar la depleción celular tras rituximab. La proteinuria de 24 horas, el complemento y los anti-ADN evalúan la actividad de la enfermedad, pero no verifican directamente el efecto del fármaco.

questions.question: In which histological class of lupus nephritis does rituximab show the greatest evidence of benefit?
questions.explanation: The most solid evidence for rituximab in lupus nephritis corresponds to proliferative classes III and IV, where its usefulness has been demonstrated in cases refractory to conventional immunosuppression. In class V (membranous) it is also used, although with less support. In classes I and VI it is not indicated.
